title: Inverse Galois Problem Resolved for Mathieu Group M₂₃ (Final Sporadic Group)
aiSystem: Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8 & OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol
whyItMatters: Constructs an explicit degree-23 polynomial in ℤ[x] realizing the Mathieu group M₂₃ over ℚ—resolving the last of the 26 sporadic finite simple groups left open since 1989.
summary: Between 1984 and 1989, mathematicians realized 25 of the 26 sporadic finite simple groups as Galois groups over ℚ, leaving only the Mathieu group M₂₃ unresolved for nearly four decades and prompting Epoch AI to include it on FrontierMath: Open Problems. On August 8, 2026 (arXiv:2608.08538), Xiaoyu Huang, Blake Jackson, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Bjorn Poonen, Rachel Pries, and Shaowu Zhang realized M₂₃ over ℚ(t) and explicitly specialized to a degree-23 polynomial in ℤ[x]. Working in a tightly human-directed collaboration with Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol multi-agent workflows—where humans chose Galois-equivariant Belyi coordinates and reduction strategies while AI accelerated code generation, data analysis, and computation orchestration—the final claims were rigorously verified without AI in Magma and PARI/GP.
technicalHighlights: Completes the 42-year program to realize all 26 sporadic finite simple groups as Galois groups over ℚ by constructing a regular M₂₃-extension of ℚ(t) and explicit degree-23 polynomial in ℤ[x].
Combines genus-4 non-hyperelliptic Hurwitz-space computations for conjugacy triple (2A, 23A, 23B) with Galois-equivariant Belyi coordinates reducing coefficient height from 10³⁶ to < 10³.
Rigorously verified in Magma and PARI/GP with public code (github.com/shaowuz/m23isgalois); upgraded by Epoch AI on Sep 16, 2026 to “Solved (human + AI)”.
caveats: Human collaborators made the decisive strategic choices (selecting Galois-equivariant coordinates and reduction algorithms when AI suggested brute-forcing higher precision); Epoch AI initially marked it human-solved on Aug 11 before updating it to “human + AI” on Sep 16 based on author accounts of AI’s instrumental workflow role.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves the final open sporadic finite simple group for the Inverse Galois Problem over ℚ after 37 years.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates a blueprint for tightly steered human–AI collaboration in explicit arithmetic geometry and Hurwitz-space computation.
scoreRationale.verification: Explicit degree-23 integer polynomial and regular cover rigorously verified in Magma and PARI/GP with open-source replication scripts; preprint undergoing journal refereeing.
scoreRationale.velocity: Final genus-4 recovery and descent computations ran in under 12 CPU-hours within a single day after multi-agent AI workflow acceleration.
